subject: Re: Northbridge Bank — security questionnaire follow-up (audit log coverage + access controls)
body:
From: Renee Chen <renee.chen@northbridgebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: IT Vendor Risk <it-vrisk@northbridgebank.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridgebank.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 8, 2025 at 2:12 PM
Subject: Northbridge Bank — security questionnaire follow-up (audit log coverage + access controls)

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the technical deep dive last week. We’re in the final pass of our vendor security questionnaire and need a bit more specificity on audit logging.

Could you confirm the following (short answers are fine, but please be explicit):

1) Coverage guarantees
- Do you guarantee 100% audit log coverage for “sensitive actions”? If yes, define what you consider sensitive actions.
- Are API key events (create/rotate/revoke), RBAC policy/role changes, and model rollout actions all captured today for Hosted + Dedicated?
- For Private deployments, are install/upgrade/rollback and config changes audited?

2) Access controls
- Who within Redwood can access customer audit logs (raw events) and under what approval process?
- Are internal accesses to customer audit logs themselves logged/audited?
- Can customers restrict access to viewing/exporting audit logs to specific admin roles?

3) Log integrity + reliability
- Do you implement tamper resistance (append-only, signing, etc.)?
- Do you have a stated delivery latency SLO (e.g., X minutes to appear/export) and alerting on drops?

4) Retention + export
- What is the default retention, and can it be configured?
- Export options (S3 / Splunk / webhook) — are these GA or beta?

If you have any existing product/security collateral that summarizes the above, please attach and we can reference it in our submission.

Thank you,
Renee

Renee Chen
Third-Party Risk & Security Assessments
Northbridge Bank



From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Renee Chen <renee.chen@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: IT Vendor Risk <it-vrisk@northbridgebank.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridgebank.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 9, 2025 at 9:03 AM
Subject: Re: Northbridge Bank — security questionnaire follow-up (audit log coverage + access controls)

Hi Renee,

Below are direct answers, and I’ve attached two short excerpts you can cite (FAQ + PRD excerpt). Happy to jump on a 15-minute call if helpful.

Attachments:
- Redwood_Audit_Logs_FAQ_Excerpt_v2025-07-09.pdf
- Audit_Logs_Enterprise_PRD_Excerpt_v2025-07-09.pdf

1) Coverage guarantees
- We are rolling out a standardized, versioned audit event schema and an explicit inventory of “sensitive actions” with enforcement to reach 100% coverage for that inventory. In our program definition, “sensitive actions” are actions that materially impact customer data access, security posture, billing, or availability (e.g., auth/RBAC changes, API keys, admin/user management, deployment/rollout actions, routing policy changes, dedicated capacity scaling/quota changes, private install/upgrade/rollback, retention changes, audit log configuration changes).
- API keys: create/rotate/revoke are audited (Hosted + Console). Dedicated uses the same identity/key system and those key lifecycle actions are audited as well.
- RBAC: role create/update/delete and permission/policy bundle changes are audited. Events include actor attribution and “what changed” diffs (with redaction of sensitive values).
- Model rollout actions: canary start/stop, pin/unpin version, and fallback/routing policy changes are audited.
- Private deployments: install/upgrade/rollback are audited with operator identity + package version + cluster identifier, and we are extending coverage for admin/config changes as part of the same sensitive-action inventory.

Notes on “guarantee”: for enterprise contracts we commit to coverage for the documented sensitive-action inventory and treat gaps as defects (tracked + fixed). If you need a specific set of events enumerated for procurement, we can provide that list.

2) Access controls
- Internal access: access to customer audit logs is restricted to a small on-call/Security Engineering subset for support/incident investigations. Access is time-bounded, requires approval, and is logged.
- Yes: internal access to audit log systems and queries are themselves logged (we log access to the audit log store and the Audit Logs API endpoints; for restricted raw access we log the approver, request ticket, and access window).
- Customer RBAC: customers can restrict viewing/exporting audit logs to admin roles. Audit log view and export are explicit permissions (not implied by general “admin” unless your org chooses to grant it).

3) Log integrity + reliability
- Integrity: audit events are written to an append-only store on our side; events are immutable once persisted. We also enforce schema validation at ingest and do not sample audit events.
- Reliability: we have delivery metrics for enqueue → persisted → exported and alerting on sustained export failures/backlog. We are finalizing a formal delivery lag SLO (targeted in minutes) and associated paging thresholds.

4) Retention + export
- Retention: default retention is environment/plan dependent; enterprise plans can configure retention windows. We can share exact defaults aligned to the SKU you’re evaluating.
- Export: S3 and webhook exports are supported; Splunk is supported via webhook/HEC-style integrations. Some sinks are GA and some are currently in enterprise beta depending on the destination and region; Naomi (cc’d) can confirm what we can enable for Northbridge during evaluation.

If you want, send the specific questionnaire language you need us to answer verbatim and we’ll respond in your format.

Best,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Renee Chen <renee.chen@northbridgebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: IT Vendor Risk <it-vrisk@northbridgebank.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridgebank.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 9, 2025 at 11:26 AM
Subject: Re: Northbridge Bank — security questionnaire follow-up (audit log coverage + access controls)

Marcus — this is helpful, thank you.

Two follow-ups based on our internal review:

A) When you say “rolling out” to reach 100% coverage, can you clarify current state vs timeline? We need to know what is available at time of contract.

B) On internal access logging: can you confirm there is an approval workflow (ticket) and that the approval + access is auditable? Our auditors often ask if vendor personnel access to logs is monitored.

Also, for retention: if we require 1 year online retention and 7 years archived to our own S3, would that be supported?

Thanks,
Renee



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Renee Chen <renee.chen@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridgebank.com>, IT Vendor Risk <it-vrisk@northbridgebank.com>
Date: Wed, Jul 9, 2025 at 1:04 PM
Subject: Re: Northbridge Bank — security questionnaire follow-up (audit log coverage + access controls)

Hi Renee,

Jumping in on (A) timeline.

- Current state (available during evaluation): audit logs are available in-product, and we already log the key event families you called out (API keys, RBAC changes, and model rollout actions). Export to customer S3/webhook can be enabled for enterprise evaluation.
- Standardization program: we’re standardizing the schema and enforcing coverage against a single “sensitive actions” inventory. That work is underway now; for enterprise contracts we can include a written list of required audited actions/events as an acceptance criterion.

If you tell us which deployment mode you’re considering (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and which regions, we can be precise about what we can enable immediately versus what’s in the next enterprise release window.

On retention: yes, 1 year online + longer-term export/archival to your S3 is a common enterprise pattern. We can confirm commercial details once we align on the plan.

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi Feldman
Director of Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference



From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Renee Chen <renee.chen@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, IT Vendor Risk <it-vrisk@northbridgebank.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbridgebank.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 10, 2025 at 9:18 AM
Subject: Re: Northbridge Bank — security questionnaire follow-up (audit log coverage + access controls)

Renee,

On (B): yes — internal restricted access is controlled via an approval workflow and ticketing.

Operationally:
- A Redwood employee must open an internal ticket stating reason (support case / incident), scope, and time window.
- Approval is required (Security/incident commander depending on context).
- Access is time-bounded and reviewed.
- We log (1) the approval record and (2) the actual access/query activity against the audit log systems.

If your auditors need evidence of that process, we can provide a redacted example of the approval record and the corresponding access log entry (showing approver + requester + timestamp + scope), under NDA.

Retention question: supporting 1 year online retention and 7 years archived to your S3 is feasible via export + customer-side retention policies. Exact controls and default retention depend on the plan; we’ll confirm in writing in the security addendum / order form.

Best,
Marcus



From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Renee Chen <renee.chen@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, IT Vendor Risk <it-vrisk@northbridgebank.com>
Date: Fri, Jul 11, 2025 at 9:41 AM
Subject: Re: Northbridge Bank — security questionnaire follow-up (audit log coverage + access controls)

Renee,

Adding an executive confirmation from our security org.

For enterprise customers, we treat audit logging as a core security control. Where there is a documented set of sensitive actions/events required for your use case, we will:
- document the required audit events (names + semantics) in the contract exhibits / security addendum,
- restrict and monitor Redwood personnel access to audit log data under an approval process, and
- treat any material gap in agreed audit coverage as a security defect with expedited remediation.

Marcus and Naomi are the right points of contact for the detailed questionnaire responses, but I wanted to confirm the posture and accountability.

Regards,
Aisha

Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
Redwood Inference
